observation_summary: The method NumberUtils.createNumber() incorrectly assumes that all hexadecimal strings should be parsed as Integers, leading to a NumberFormatException when the input string represents a value larger than Integer.MAX_VALUE.
reasoning_summary: The defect lies in the procedural logic of createNumber() (lines 471-474), which uses an incorrect threshold (8 hex digits) to decide whether to call createInteger(). Because the logic for determining the appropriate numeric type (Integer vs Long) is flawed for hex strings, it is an algorithmic error in the conversion strategy. It is not a missing guard (Checking) because the logic exists but is wrong, and it is not a simple assignment error.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not a missing guard, but an incorrect threshold logic that determines which method to call for conversion.
This is a local procedural logic error within an existing method, not a missing capability or design-level omission.
